name: Kettlemore Yards
description:
A sprawling mid-tier industrial district wedged between two elevated transit corridors on GLMZ's northwest fringe, Kettlemore Yards was originally a Ringo Heavy Industries fabrication campus repurposed after the company's 2178 restructuring left the site contractually ungoverned. Over the following two decades, hundreds of small-scale manufacturers, unlicensed fabricators, and gray-market machine shops colonized the enormous corrugated sheds and loading bays, creating a chaotic but functional ecosystem of production. The Yards now output everything from licensed agricultural equipment to bespoke weapon components, often within the same building.

The district's defining feature is its permanent atmospheric haze — a combination of metal particulate, vented coolant steam, and the acrid output of dozens of unlicensed smelters running around the clock. Residents and workers universally wear filter masks outdoors, and the local slang for the haze is simply 'the weather.' Tier 2 and 3 workers live in converted storage structures inside the Yards perimeter, and a densely packed commercial strip called Smoke Row runs along the southern fence line, offering food stalls, tool shops, body modification parlors, and every variety of informal service.

sights: Plumes of white and gray-yellow steam rise constantly from corrugated shed vents, merging into a low ceiling of industrial haze that diffuses the overhead glow of the elevated transit lines.
Modified cargo drones move in loose swarms between shed rooftops, ferrying components between fabrication stations too crowded for ground-level transport.
Workers in scorched coveralls and welding masks move in and out of shed doors that glow orange from the forge fires inside.
Smoke Row's stall lights — cheap neon and bioluminescent strips — bleed color into the haze in streaks of pink and green.
sounds: A constant layered percussion of stamping presses, grinders, and pneumatic hammers reverberates through the corrugated walls and carries across the entire district.
Cargo drone swarms produce a collective buzzing hum that rises and falls as clusters pass overhead.
Smoke Row is perpetually loud with vendor calls, the hiss of food stalls, and the overlapping music bleeding from a dozen different establishments.
smells: Hot metal and ozone from active welding and plasma cutting is the district's baseline smell, present everywhere.
Vented coolant fluid adds a sharp synthetic sweetness that hits the back of the throat.
Smoke Row contributes waves of grilling protein, fry oil, and cheap spice blends that briefly overpower the industrial background.
atmosphere.feel: Kettlemore Yards operates at a relentless, slightly anxious pitch — everyone is working, hustling, or moving product. The air itself feels used. There is a rough solidarity among long-term residents who share the same environmental exposure and the same distrust of outside authority, but new arrivals are watched carefully until proven useful or at least harmless.

demographics: Predominantly Tier 2-3 workers of South Asian, East African, and Central American descent, reflecting the migrant labor waves that originally staffed the Ringo campus. A significant population of unlicensed synthetic workers operates semi-openly here.
economy: The Yards runs on fabrication contracts — legitimate, gray, and black — with Smoke Row providing a secondary service economy. Ringo Heavy Industries retains a nominal licensing claim on the district that it occasionally leverages for a cut of larger operations.
power_structure: The Shed Bosses — a loose association of the twelve largest fabrication operators — collectively manage district access and resolve disputes, but Ringo's regional compliance officer maintains a quiet veto over anything that draws too much scrutiny.
dangers: Unlicensed smelter explosions and chemical venting incidents occur several times a year, and emergency response is slow and expensive.
Arcturus Defense Solutions runs periodic sweeps for unlicensed weapons fabrication; tipped-off operators disappear before the raids, but the tippers remain unknown.
Rival fabrication crews occasionally escalate contract disputes into direct sabotage or worse.
Long-term particulate exposure causes significant respiratory degradation — the local clinics are overwhelmed and underfunded.
opportunities: The Yards can produce almost any physical component if you know which shed to approach and what currency to offer — including things that don't appear in any catalog.
The synthetic worker population is large, organized, and looking for outside allies willing to help navigate the personhood legislation moving through the GLMZ civic council.

A gray-market data broker operating out of a Smoke Row noodle stall has access to Ringo's original campus schematics, which reportedly show several sub-basement levels that don't appear on current maps.
story_hooks: Three fabricators from different sheds have independently gone missing in the past month, all of them specialists in a particular class of Zheng-Dao Bioelectric power cell. The Shed Bosses are quietly funding an investigation because they can't afford the attention of going to Ferrogate Security.

A synthetic worker named Provisional-7 — known locally as Sev — has been running an unauthorized mutual aid network inside the Yards for two years, stockpiling fabricated medical equipment for the district's clinics. Ringo's compliance officer has just become aware of this and wants the network dismantled before it becomes a news story; Sev is looking for extraction help before the Bosses are pressured into compliance.

A fire in Shed 14 last week was ruled an accident, but the shed's entire output for the past six months — the nature of which nobody will specify — was destroyed, and the owner has since vanished. The cargo insurer is offering Φ15,000 for documentation of what was actually being made there.
frequented_by: Gray-market fabricators and machine shop operators
Body modification specialists catering to industrial workers

notable_locations.name: Smoke Row
notable_locations.description: A dense commercial strip along the Yards' southern fence line packed with food stalls, tool vendors, body mod parlors, and informal service providers.

notable_locations.name: Shed 1 — The Anchor
notable_locations.description: The largest and oldest fabrication shed, now divided among six competing operators who maintain an uneasy shared truce over its common equipment.
